question: Urine osmolality in Diabetes insipidus is
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Diabetes insipidus" -> "decreased ADH effect" -> "inability to concentrate urine" -> "dilute urine" -> "low urine osmolality" -> "<300 mmol/L" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Diabetes insipidus" -> "polyuria" -> "excessive water loss" -> "dilute urine" -> "low urine osmolality" -> "<150 mmol/L" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Diabetes insipidus" -> "impaired water reabsorption" -> "dilute urine" -> "low urine osmolality" -> "<600 mmol/L" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Diabetes insipidus" -> "lack of ADH" -> "inability to concentrate urine" -> "dilute urine" -> "low urine osmolality" -> "<900 mmol/L" -> 60%
analysis: Diabetes insipidus is characterized by the inability of the kidneys to concentrate urine due to a deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or a lack of response to it. This results in the production of large volumes of dilute urine. Typically, urine osmolality in diabetes insipidus is low, often less than 300 mmol/L, as the kidneys are unable to concentrate the urine effectively.
